Thursday gave back part of Wednesday's follow-through — SPY −0.35% and QQQ −0.32% held above their rally-attempt lows while small caps lagged −1.64% — and the tape split around the NVDA shock: AMD and AVGO ripped higher on the rotation while NVDA itself fell another 4.34% on 4.5x volume the day its CEO stepped down.

Market — SPY · QQQ · IWM · TLT

Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
Thursday gave back part of Wednesday's follow-through — SPY −0.35% to 757.12 and QQQ −0.32% to 688.17, both holding above their rally-attempt lows, while IWM fell 1.64% and TLT 1.48% — and the day's real story was the split the NVDA shock created. NVDA itself fell another 4.34% to 166.19 on 4.49x volume, the day Jensen stepped down: Prof calls him “former NVIDIA CEO” and supplies the oversold study — daily RSI 25, the lowest since May 2019, with 11 prior RSI(14) ≤ 25 readings showing 82% higher one year later at an average +33.4% — plus the volume scoreboard (30-day average 163 million, Thursday 672 million, “thats 4x volume”). Sean supplies the tape: a gap-down open at 151.01, a low of 148.80, a recovery to 166.19, and his own trade — he sold $135 puts for Nov 20. DiCarlo supplies the contrarian read: “one of the biggest stop hunts on retail in decades… big money bought the dip, and they seem to think the stock will be just fine” — and “why I think we hit all-time highs in 6 months.” But the money that left NVDA did not leave the tape: AMD rose another 5.86% to 585.30 and AVGO 5.54% to 364.36, and Remz supplies the rotation call — “hard not to be bullish on chip names like $AMD, $AVGO, and $DELL” — plus his #1 year-end name, AVGO, with the double bottom at 290, the 200-day being reclaimed at 367, “long over 381” and “short under 335”. The indexes held up through it: Enrich supplies the read — “Market absorbed the NVDA headlines reasonably well, but small caps lagged. Resilient indexes, uneven participation” — and his QQQ hurdle: the second close above $687 “clears our $684 hurdle. Now we need consolidation here, higher.” DiCarlo supplies the SPY read: it “bounced perfectly off our Daily Smart Money Zone. Up 3.5%+ since the pullback. Now it's running into an extremely important resistance. What happens here decides what comes next.” The third convergence is Unity: iain, Enrich and Venu all land on $U on the same day — iain with the 1,600+ day base and “> 50, this thing could really get moving”, Enrich with the $55 calls for Dec 18 (“one of my favorite setups on the market right now”), Venu with the power earnings gap out of the base — and the close, 50.18, is above 50 with the 52-week high 51.49 as the trigger. Venu supplies the same pattern three more times — SPOT, YOU and TMDX as “the best-looking early Stage 2 names in the current market”, all power earnings gap breakouts — though SPOT is the cautionary one: Sean added through 609 and Venu's chart shows the same 609.88 base top, but the close 598.51 fell back under it. The earnings tape added a fourth split: NBIS fell 16.84% on a quarter where sales grew 571% — DiCarlo still calls it a long-term buy and Prof points to the broken 135 support — while AMAT beat and raised guidance after the close (record $10.41B revenue, +53%; adj. EPS $4.16 vs $4.06) and held roughly flat after hours. Your process gives three genuine qualifiers with triggers above the close: U (three traders, base breakout, trigger 51.49), ZETA (testing its highs, trigger 37.74) and YOU (PEG breakout, trigger 65.72) — plus AVGO as a reclaim in progress (long over 381) and SPOT as a breakout that failed to hold. The extended names tell the other half: AMD (+5.86% on top of Wednesday's +7.32% and the after-hours leg), AAPL at its highs, and DELL — “exploding” at midday per Remz, closed −0.67%. The discipline is in the framing: the follow-through held its first down day and QQQ cleared Enrich's hurdle, but the leadership question now runs through the rotation names — and Friday's open, with Enrich calling “a classic $TSLA Friday”, is the next test.

  • Badge key: Setup describes structure only (green = constructive, amber = pending confirmation, red = broken/extended/avoid). Coverage counts the traders behind a name and is always gray — “Chart only” means no trader mentioned it and implies nothing about the setup. The stage pill next to each ticker (30-week MA basis) is the only place a stage label appears; it is kept out of the prose and the setup badges, and traders' own quoted words are exempt.
  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels. AVGO's trigger 381.00 and invalidation 335.00 are Remz's chart levels; U's invalidation 48.20 is Venu's chart line; YOU's trigger 65.72 and TMDX's trigger 97.54 are Venu's chart levels; SPOT's trigger 609.00 is Sean's stated level; ZETA's and U's triggers are their 52-week highs.
